thread:
incident-bot: Pager: Dedicated capacity p99 latency breach detected for region-us-west-2. Alert: DEDICATED_P99_SLO_BREACH threshold=5s current=18.2s queue_depth=312
Alex C.: seeing lots of streaming stalls reported in logs, p95 also creeping up (~4.1s) but p99 is brutal
Maria L.: confirmed — dashboards show queue depth spike starting ~03:12 UTC, sustained through now. Autoscaler not adding new nodes.
Devon K.: tagging this as Sev2 for now, customer-impacting for dedicated tenants using low-latency route.
Lee (SRE): I'm on pager, pulling metrics now. Which tenants are on the dedicated pool?
Samira R.: acme-inc, lumos-ai and fintechco on that pool. CS already opened a ticket with acme.
Alex C.: logs show warmup failures: new instances report `KV cache miss` and `model shard mapping pending` for ~30s each. Warmup timeout is 20s currently.
EngOps Bot: autoscaler events: 03:12:07 scale-request queued, 03:12:09 scale-request failed (timeout), 03:13:45 attempted scale to +2 GPUs, provisioning delayed by cloud spot reclaim wait.
Devon K.: so autoscaler issued requests but backend instances didn't become available fast enough -> cold start tail latency. Need mitigation to reduce queue and restore SLOs.
Lee (SRE): immediate mitigation options: 1) manual capacity bump with on-demand instances 2) route affected tenants to hosted fallback model 3) throttle new requests / shed low-priority traffic. Thoughts?
Maria L.: recommend 2 + 3 first to minimize customer impact while we get nodes up. Can we flip routing rule for acme-inc only?
Alex C.: yes, we have per-tenant routing policy. I can push a rule to route acme-inc and lumos-ai to hosted-inference-1 (latency ~60-80ms) as fallback. finTechCo has stricter compliance — need CS signoff.
Samira R.: I'm on CS thread with finTechCo; they said allow fallback if preserving model version and logs. opt-in via consent recorded in ticket.
oncall-bot: On-call handoff: @Lee (SRE) is the primary; if additional escalation needed, page @Devon K.
Lee (SRE): performing quick triage: grabbing p99 tail traces. Also checking streaming worker logs for stalls.
Alex C.: paste: ```
queue_depth by pod: pod-4: 88, pod-2: 79, pod-7: 65, pod-3: 40, pod-5: 40
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.12
streaming_stall_count_last_5m: 142
```
Devon K.: that hit rate is terrible. Might be that the cache priming job didn't run on new nodes. Are we evicting caches on scale events?
Maria L.: recent deploy modified cache eviction settings; default max-age lowered and `--prime-on-attach` flag not set in recipe. That would explain cold misses on attach.
Lee (SRE): I'm going to temporarily increase warmup timeout to 90s to let nodes finish priming, and manually request 3 on-demand GPUs for the pool. Alex, can you prepare the routing change?
Alex C.: preparing routing change now. Patch: `routes add --tenant acme-inc,lumos-ai --to hosted-inference-1 --preserve-model-version` will be applied.
EngOps Bot: manual scale command executed by Lee: `redwood scale dedicated-pool-usw2 --count +3 --type on-demand` request-id=scale-1829
Alex C.: routing rule applied. Confirmed 200 responses for test requests to acme-inc via hosted-inference-1. :white_check_mark:
Samira R.: finTechCo still pending consent, holding off on fallback. CS pinged legal, ETA ~10m.
Lee (SRE): on-demand nodes are provisioning. ETA showing ~5m on cloud console but networking handshake may add time. Increasing warmup timeout now.
Devon K.: while we wait, enable token-based request prioritization and shed background eval traffic (route id: evals). Can someone run the throttle?
Alex C.: running throttle: `rlimit set --pool dedicated-pool-usw2 --priority low --rate 10rps` applied.
Maria L.: after throttle and routing, p95 dropped to 2.1s and p99 to 6.2s (still above SLO but improving). Queue depth down to ~70 total.
Lee (SRE): on-demand nodes now ready and attached, cache priming logs show successful priming with `--prime-on-attach=true` set for these instances. p99 now 3.8s.
Devon K.: good. We should also revert the recent cache eviction change in the recipe and schedule a rollout with canary and prime-on-attach in staging.
Alex C.: filing PR now to restore previous eviction settings and add integration test for prime-on-attach behavior. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/4981
Samira R.: customer-impact summary for CS: acme-inc: intermittent degraded latency 03:12-03:31 (19m), lumos-ai: similar 03:12-03:29 (17m), finTechCo: partial degraded queueing 03:12-03:17 (5m) — no data loss reported.
CS-Bot: created incident ticket INC-2026-3408 and linked customer contacts.
Lee (SRE): putting incident into mitigation state. On-call handoff at 03:40UTC to @Devon K. for postmortem and remediation.
Devon K.: taking handoff. Next actions: postmortem timeline, change to warmup defaults, autoscaler retry/backoff tuning, include on-demand fallback in autoscaler policy, add more visible warmup success metric in console.
Maria L.: logging snippet for postmortem: `autoscaler: retry_count=4 backoff=30s provision_time=320s spot_preempt=true` — need to detect prolonged provisioning and fallback immediately.
Alex C.: export of latency graphs attached to incident ticket.
Lee (SRE): final status: mitigation successful, p99 back under 5s after manual scale + routing + throttling. Leaving this thread open for postmortem notes.
Devon K.: noted. I'll draft the postmortem and ping folks for action items. Thanks all. :heart:
